For example, in the score_pids method, you could add code to save Q and the document embeddings (D_packed) before computing the score. That way, you can use the exported tensors to train your CNN in place of the existing cosine (dot product) logic.

Here's a sketch of how you might modify the GPU branch in score_pids:

````python
def score_pids(self, config, Q, pids, centroid_scores):
    # ...existing code...

    # Rank final list of docs using full approximate embeddings (including residuals)
    if self.use_gpu:
        D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
        
        # EXPORT Q (query tensor) and D_packed (document tensor) for CNN training
        torch.save(Q, "extracted_query_tensor.pt")
        torch.save(D_packed, "extracted_doc_tensor.pt")
    else:
        D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
                pids,
                self.doclens,
                self.offsets,
                self.codec.bucket_weights,
                self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
                self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
                self.embeddings.residuals,
                self.embeddings.codes,
                self.codec.centroids,
                self.codec.dim,
                self.codec.nbits
            )
        D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
        D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]

    # ...existing code continues...
    if Q.size(0) == 1:
        return colbert_score_packed(Q, D_packed, D_mask, config), pids

    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()

    return colbert_score(Q, D_padded, D_lengths, config), pids
````

With these changes, you’ll have the tensors used in the cosine similarity computation on disk so that your CNN can be trained to replace that logic.

ColBERT pre-normalizes both its query (Q) and document (D) embeddings so that a dot product becomes equivalent to a cosine similarity. During retrieval, after candidate generation, the query is encoded into Q (via the Searcher.encode method) and then passed to score_pids (see colbert/search/index_storage.py). In score_pids, the document embeddings (D_packed) are obtained (using lookup_pids or decompressed from residuals) and are normalized. Then the functions colbert_score_packed or colbert_score (defined in colbert/modeling/colbert.py) compute the dot product between Q and D_packed, which is equivalent to computing cosine similarity.

If you want to train a CNN to replace this cosine logic, you can export the Q and D_packed tensors right before the call to colbert_score_packed/colbert_score in score_pids. This gives you the exact pre-cosine (i.e. pre-dot-product) representations for your CNN training.

Then the functions colbert_score_packed or colbert_score (defined in [colbert/modeling/colbert.py](colbert/modeling/colbert.py)) compute the dot product between Q and D_packed, which is equivalent to computing cosine similarity.

The Q tensor is produced by the query encoder and typically has the shape

  [num_queries, query_maxlen, embedding_dim]

where each query is represented as a sequence of token embeddings (with query_maxlen tokens, each having embedding_dim dimensions).

Similarly, the D_packed tensor (from lookup_pids) represents the document or passage embeddings and has a shape

  [num_docs, doc_token_length, embedding_dim]

Here, doc_token_length may vary (or be padded to a fixed maximum) so that each token in the document is represented in the same embedding_dim space.

Below is an example of modifying your Searcher class so that every key method immediately prints a debug message. This way you can verify that the correct methods are actually being called. For example, in your [searcher.py](colbert/searcher.py) file, you could update the methods as follows:

````python
# filepath: /home/st1084516/ColBERT-Thesis/colbert/searcher.py
class Searcher:
    def __init__(self, index, checkpoint=None, collection=None, config=None, index_root=None, verbose:int = 3):
        self.verbose = verbose
        print(f"DEBUG: __init__ called in Searcher ({__file__})", flush=True)
        if self.verbose > 1:
            print_memory_stats()

        initial_config = ColBERTConfig.from_existing(config, Run().config)
        default_index_root = initial_config.index_root_
        index_root = index_root if index_root else default_index_root
        self.index = os.path.join(index_root, index)
        self.index_config = ColBERTConfig.load_from_index(self.index)

        self.checkpoint = checkpoint or self.index_config.checkpoint
        self.checkpoint_config = ColBERTConfig.load_from_checkpoint(self.checkpoint)
        self.config = ColBERTConfig.from_existing(self.checkpoint_config, self.index_config, initial_config)

        self.collection = Collection.cast(collection or self.config.collection)
        self.configure(checkpoint=self.checkpoint, collection=self.collection)

        self.checkpoint = Checkpoint(self.checkpoint, colbert_config=self.config, verbose=self.verbose)
        use_gpu = self.config.total_visible_gpus > 0
        if use_gpu:
            self.checkpoint = self.checkpoint.cuda()
        load_index_with_mmap = self.config.load_index_with_mmap
        if load_index_with_mmap and use_gpu:
            raise ValueError("Memory-mapped index can only be used with CPU!")
        self.ranker = IndexScorer(self.index, use_gpu, load_index_with_mmap)

        print("DEBUG: Completed __init__ in Searcher", flush=True)
        print_memory_stats()

    def configure(self, **kw_args):
        print("DEBUG: Entered configure", flush=True)
        self.config.configure(**kw_args)

    def encode(self, text: TextQueries, full_length_search=False):
        print("DEBUG: Entered encode", flush=True)
        queries = text if isinstance(text, list) else [text]
        bsize = 128 if len(queries) > 128 else None

        self.checkpoint.query_tokenizer.query_maxlen = self.config.query_maxlen
        Q = self.checkpoint.queryFromText(queries, bsize=bsize, to_cpu=True, full_length_search=full_length_search)
        print(f"DEBUG: Returning tensor Q of shape {Q.shape} from encode", flush=True)
        return Q

    def search(self, text: str, k=10, filter_fn=None, full_length_search=False, pids=None):
        print("DEBUG: Entered search", flush=True)
        Q = self.encode(text, full_length_search=full_length_search)
        return self.dense_search(Q, k, filter_fn=filter_fn, pids=pids)

    def search_all(self, queries: TextQueries, k=10, filter_fn=None, full_length_search=False, qid_to_pids=None):
        print("DEBUG: Entered search_all", flush=True)
        queries = Queries.cast(queries)
        queries_ = list(queries.values())
        Q = self.encode(queries_, full_length_search=full_length_search)
        return self._search_all_Q(queries, Q, k, filter_fn=filter_fn, qid_to_pids=qid_to_pids)

    def _search_all_Q(self, queries, Q, k, filter_fn=None, qid_to_pids=None):
        print("DEBUG: Entered _search_all_Q", flush=True)
        qids = list(queries.keys())
        if qid_to_pids is None:
            qid_to_pids = {qid: None for qid in qids}

        all_scored_pids = [
            list(zip(*self.dense_search(
                Q[query_idx:query_idx+1],
                k, filter_fn=filter_fn,
                pids=qid_to_pids[qid]
            )))
            for query_idx, qid in enumerate(qids)
        ]
        print("DEBUG: Completed dense_search calls in _search_all_Q", flush=True)
        data = {qid: val for qid, val in zip(queries.keys(), all_scored_pids)}

        provenance = Provenance()
        provenance.source = 'Searcher::search_all'
        provenance.queries = queries.provenance()
        provenance.config = self.config.export()
        provenance.k = k

        return Ranking(data=data, provenance=provenance)

    def dense_search(self, Q: torch.Tensor, k=10, filter_fn=None, pids=None):
        print("DEBUG: Entered dense_search", flush=True)
        # Configuration branch based on k.
        if k <= 10:
            if self.config.ncells is None:
                self.configure(ncells=1)
            if self.config.centroid_score_threshold is None:
                self.configure(centroid_score_threshold=0.5)
            if self.config.ndocs is None:
                self.configure(ndocs=256)
        elif k <= 100:
            if self.config.ncells is None:
                self.configure(ncells=2)
            if self.config.centroid_score_threshold is None:
                self.configure(centroid_score_threshold=0.45)
            if self.config.ndocs is None:
                self.configure(ndocs=1024)
        else:
            if self.config.ncells is None:
                self.configure(ncells=4)
            if self.config.centroid_score_threshold is None:
                self.configure(centroid_score_threshold=0.4)
            if self.config.ndocs is None:
                self.configure(ndocs=max(k * 4, 4096))

        pids, scores = self.ranker.rank(self.config, Q, filter_fn=filter_fn, pids=pids)
        print(f"DEBUG: dense_search returning {len(pids)} pids and {len(scores)} scores", flush=True)
        return pids[:k], list(range(1, k+1)), scores[:k]
````

response.value:
That error suggests that inside your checkpoint’s queryFromText method, the code is trying to access a tensor attribute (self.query.shape) but instead self.query is actually a function. In other words, the name "query" in your checkpoint object is shadowing what you expect to be a tensor.

Here’s how you might debug and fix it:

1. In your queryFromText method (in checkpoint.py), add a debug print for the type of self.query. For example:
  
    ````python
    print(f"DEBUG: type(self.query): {type(self.query)}", flush=True)
    ````
  
   This will tell you if self.query is indeed a function rather than a tensor.

2. Check your checkpoint initialization to ensure that you’re not accidentally assigning a function (perhaps the query method itself) to the attribute self.query. There might be a naming conflict—if the method queryFromText and an attribute query share the same name, Python might be confused about which one to call.

3. Consider renaming either the attribute or the method if they conflict. For example, if self.query is meant to hold the query tensor, verify that it’s assigned correctly. If it’s instead supposed to be a method, then change the attribute name so that your code accessing self.query.shape will work as expected on the tensor.

By following these steps you should be able to determine why self.query is a function and fix the naming or assignment so that it’s the tensor you expect.

To export the query and document tensors before the “packing” (i.e. before further processing with StridedTensor), you can add export (e.g. using torch.save) right after calling lookup_pids (in the GPU branch), before any extra reshaping or normalization. For example, modify score_pids like this:

````python

def score_pids(self, config, Q, pids, centroid_scores):
    global counter
    batch_size = 2 ** 20

    print("DEBUG: Entered score_pids", flush=True)

    if centroid_scores is not None:
        print("score_pids: Using centroid_scores branch")
        if self.use_gpu:
            print("score_pids: GPU enabled in centroid_scores branch")
            centroid_scores = centroid_scores.cuda()
        idx = centroid_scores.max(-1).values >= config.centroid_score_threshold
        print(f"score_pids: Centroid threshold filter applied, idx shape: {idx.shape}")
        if self.use_gpu:
            print("score_pids: Processing approx_scores on GPU")
            approx_scores = []
            for i in range(0, ceil(len(pids) / batch_size)):
                print(f"score_pids: Processing batch {i}")
                pids_ = pids[i * batch_size : (i+1) * batch_size]
                codes_packed, codes_lengths = self.embeddings_strided.lookup_codes(pids_)
                idx_ = idx[codes_packed.long()]
                pruned_codes_strided = StridedTensor(idx_, codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
                pruned_codes_padded, pruned_codes_mask = pruned_codes_strided.as_padded_tensor()
                pruned_codes_lengths = (pruned_codes_padded * pruned_codes_mask).sum(dim=1)
                codes_packed_ = codes_packed[idx_]
                approx_scores_ = centroid_scores[codes_packed_.long()]
                if approx_scores_.shape[0] == 0:
                    approx_scores.append(torch.zeros((len(pids_),), dtype=approx_scores_.dtype).cuda())
                    continue
                approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores_, pruned_codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
                approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
                approx_scores_ = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
                approx_scores.append(approx_scores_)
            approx_scores = torch.cat(approx_scores, dim=0)
            assert approx_scores.is_cuda, approx_scores.device
            if config.ndocs < len(approx_scores):
                print("score_pids: Applying topk for pruned docs")
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=config.ndocs).indices]
            codes_packed, codes_lengths = self.embeddings_strided.lookup_codes(pids)
            approx_scores = centroid_scores[codes_packed.long()]
            approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores, codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
            approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
            approx_scores = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
            if config.ndocs // 4 < len(approx_scores):
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=(config.ndocs // 4)).indices]
        else:
            print("score_pids: CPU branch for centroid_scores")
            pids = IndexScorer.filter_pids(
                pids, centroid_scores, self.embeddings.codes, self.doclens,
                self.offsets, idx, config.ndocs
            )
    else:
        print("score_pids: centroid_scores is None")
    
    # Export before further "packing" (i.e. before passing to StridedTensor for padded formatting)
    if self.use_gpu:
        print("score_pids: Using GPU for final ranking")
        D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
        # Export raw tensors before any reshaping/packing is done.
        torch.save(Q, "exported_query_pre_pack.pt")
        torch.save(D_packed, "exported_doc_pre_pack.pt")
    else:
        print("score_pids: Using CPU for final ranking")
        D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
            pids,
            self.doclens,
            self.offsets,
            self.codec.bucket_weights,
            self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
            self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
            self.embeddings.residuals,
            self.embeddings.codes,
            self.codec.centroids,
            self.codec.dim,
            self.codec.nbits
        )
        D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
        D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]

    counter += 1
    print(f"Counter: {counter}")
    print(f"score_pids: D_packed shape: {D_packed.shape}")
    print(f"score_pids: Q shape: {Q.shape}")
    if Q.size(0) == 1:
        print("score_pids: Using colbert_score_packed")
        return colbert_score_packed(Q, D_packed, D_mask, config), pids

    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()
    print("score_pids: Using colbert_score")
    return colbert_score(Q, D_padded, D_lengths, config), pids
````

In this change, immediately after obtaining the raw output of lookup_pids (which produces D_packed with shape [29526, 128] in your case), we export Q and D_packed by saving them to disk (using torch.save).  

Keep in mind that lookup_pids returns a flattened (packed) tensor along with a mask. If you need the original per-document token representations (i.e. before flattening), you’d need to “unpack” them using D_mask (which you should have from lookup_pids) to reshape each document embedding back to its original token count. For example, you could reconstruct a list of document embeddings like this:

````python
doc_embeddings = []
offset = 0
for length in D_mask:
    doc_embeddings.append(D_packed[offset:offset + length].clone())
    offset += length
torch.save(doc_embeddings, "exported_doc_raw_list.pt")
````

Adjust according to your needs.

This export happens before the StridedTensor is applied to pack the document embeddings for scoring, so you can use these exported tensors to train your CNN or for any other purpose.

                approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores_, pruned_codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
                approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
                approx_scores_ = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
                approx_scores.append(approx_scores_)
            approx_scores = torch.cat(approx_scores, dim=0)
            assert approx_scores.is_cuda, approx_scores.device
            if config.ndocs < len(approx_scores):
                print("score_pids: Applying topk for pruned docs")
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=config.ndocs).indices]
            codes_packed, codes_lengths = self.embeddings_strided.lookup_codes(pids)
            approx_scores = centroid_scores[codes_packed.long()]
            approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores, codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
            approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
            approx_scores = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
            if config.ndocs // 4 < len(approx_scores):
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=(config.ndocs // 4)).indices]
        else:
            print("score_pids: CPU branch for centroid_scores")
            pids = IndexScorer.filter_pids(
                pids, centroid_scores, self.embeddings.codes, self.doclens,
                self.offsets, idx, config.ndocs
            )
    else:
        print("score_pids: centroid_scores is None")
    
    # Export before further "packing" (i.e. before passing to StridedTensor for padded formatting)
    if self.use_gpu:
        print("score_pids: Using GPU for final ranking")
        D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
        # Export raw tensors before any reshaping/packing is done.
        torch.save(Q, "exported_query_pre_pack.pt")
        torch.save(D_packed, "exported_doc_pre_pack.pt")
    else:
        print("score_pids: Using CPU for final ranking")
        D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
            pids,
            self.doclens,
            self.offsets,
            self.codec.bucket_weights,
            self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
            self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
            self.embeddings.residuals,
            self.embeddings.codes,
            self.codec.centroids,
            self.codec.dim,
            self.codec.nbits
        )
        D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
        D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]

    counter += 1
    print(f"Counter: {counter}")
    print(f"score_pids: D_packed shape: {D_packed.shape}")
    print(f"score_pids: Q shape: {Q.shape}")
    if Q.size(0) == 1:
        print("score_pids: Using colbert_score_packed")
        return colbert_score_packed(Q, D_packed, D_mask, config), pids

    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()
    print("score_pids: Using colbert_score")
    return colbert_score(Q, D_padded, D_lengths, config), pids

Keep in mind that lookup_pids returns a flattened (packed) tensor along with a mask. If you need the original per-document token representations (i.e. before flattening), you’d need to “unpack” them using D_mask (which you should have from lookup_pids) to reshape each document embedding back to its original token count. For example, you could reconstruct a list of document embeddings like this:

````python
doc_embeddings = []
offset = 0
for length in D_mask:
    doc_embeddings.append(D_packed[offset:offset + length].clone())
    offset += length
torch.save(doc_embeddings, "exported_doc_raw_list.pt")
````

Specifically, after retrieving D_packed and D_mask, use:

 D_strided, then call its as_padded_tensor() method to recover the padded document tensor.

For example, modify your GPU branch in score_pids as follows:

````python

    print("score_pids: Using GPU for final ranking")
    print(f"score_pids: pids shape: {pids.shape}", flush=True)
    D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
    
    # Convert the packed document embeddings to padded form.
    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()  # D_padded shape: [num_docs, max_tokens, emb_dim]
    
    # Export the non-packed (padded) document embeddings.
    torch.save(D_padded, "exported_doc_padded.pt")
    torch.save(D_lengths, "exported_doc_lengths.pt")
else:
    # CPU branch (similar conversion)
    D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
        pids,
        self.doclens,
        self.offsets,
        self.codec.bucket_weights,
        self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
        self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
        self.embeddings.residuals,
        self.embeddings.codes,
        self.codec.centroids,
        self.codec.dim,
        self.codec.nbits
    )
    D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
    D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]
    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()
    torch.save(D_padded, "exported_doc_padded.pt")
    torch.save(D_lengths, "exported_doc_lengths.pt")
````

message.text: why the StridedTensor ?

parts.text: why the StridedTensor ?

response.value: The StridedTensor is a helper class that converts existing (often uneven or "packed") document representations into a padded tensor format along with an appropriate mask. In ColBERT, documents can have variable lengths (i.e. different token counts), and initially the document embeddings are stored in a flat format. The StridedTensor takes this flat representation and the token-lengths mask (D_mask) and produces a dense tensor (D_padded) with a consistent shape (e.g. [num_docs, max_tokens, emb_dim]). This padded format is necessary for computing similarity scores (e.g. via colbert_score) where the dimensions need to align properly for operations like dot product or cosine similarity.

message.text: so what is the reconstruct the original variable-length document representations.

parts.text: so what is the reconstruct the original variable-length document representations.

response.value:
The "reconstruction" of the original variable-length document representations means taking the padded tensor (which has a fixed maximum token length for all documents) and using the associated lengths (or mask) to recover the actual token embeddings for each document.

For example, given:

• D_padded with shape [num_docs, max_tokens, emb_dim]

• D_lengths with shape [num_docs] (containing the true number of tokens per document)

You can reconstruct a list of document embeddings (one per document) like this:

````python
doc_embeddings = [D_padded[i, :int(D_lengths[i])] for i in range(D_padded.shape[0])]
````

Each element in `doc_embeddings` is a tensor of shape `[valid_tokens, emb_dim]` corresponding to the original variable-length embedding for that document. This way, even though internally the embeddings are stored in a padded, fixed-shape tensor, you can recover the original variable-length representations using the associated lengths or mask.

Below is a snippet you can insert into your score_pids function (for example, immediately after the lookup and before the final scoring) to export the tensors for CNN training. This snippet converts the flat D_packed and associated mask into a padded document tensor, then saves Q, D_padded, and D_lengths:

````python
# After obtaining D_packed and D_mask, convert to padded format.

if self.use_gpu:
    print("score_pids: Using GPU for final ranking", flush=True)
    print(f"score_pids: pids shape: {pids.shape}", flush=True)
    D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
else:
    print("score_pids: Using CPU for final ranking", flush=True)
    D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
        pids,
        self.doclens,
        self.offsets,
        self.codec.bucket_weights,
        self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
        self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
        self.embeddings.residuals,
        self.embeddings.codes,
        self.codec.centroids,
        self.codec.dim,
        self.codec.nbits
    )
    D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
    D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]

# Convert the flat embeddings and mask into padded (non-packed) representation.
D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()  # D_padded: [num_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]

# Export the Query and Document tensors for CNN training.
torch.save(Q, "exported_query.pt")                   # Expected shape: [1, query_maxlen, emb_dim] e.g., [1, 32, 128]
torch.save(D_padded, "exported_doc_padded.pt")         # Expected shape: [num_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]
torch.save(D_lengths, "exported_doc_lengths.pt")       # Expected shape: [num_docs]
print("Exported Q, D_padded, and D_lengths for CNN training", flush=True)
````

### How It Works

1. **Lookup & Conversion:**  
   Whether on GPU or CPU, the code first obtains D_packed and D_mask, then uses the StridedTensor helper to convert these into a padded tensor D_padded (with shape [num_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]) and D_lengths that records each document’s true token count.

2. **Exporting:**  
   The query tensor Q is saved (its shape is the same as produced by the query encoder, e.g., [1, 32, 128]).  
   The exported document tensor, D_padded, preserves the per-document structure so that each document is represented as a sequence of token embeddings.  
   D_lengths is saved so you can later reconstruct the true variable-length representation if needed.

3. **Usage:**  
   These exported tensors can then be loaded into your CNN training script to replace cosine-similarity scoring.

Place this snippet at the appropriate point in your score_pids function, and the exported files will be written where your script is run.

````python
def score_pids(self, config, Q, pids, centroid_scores):
    """
        Always supply a flat list or tensor for `pids`.
        Supply sizes Q = (1 | num_docs, *, dim) and D = (num_docs, *, dim).
        If Q.size(0) is 1, the matrix will be compared with all passages.
        Otherwise, each query matrix will be compared against the *aligned* passage.
    """
    global counter

    # TODO: Remove batching?
    batch_size = 2 ** 20

    print("DEBUG: Entered score_pids", flush=True)

    if centroid_scores is not None:
        print("score_pids: Using centroid_scores branch", flush=True)
        if self.use_gpu:
            print("score_pids: GPU enabled in centroid_scores branch", flush=True)
            centroid_scores = centroid_scores.cuda()

        idx = centroid_scores.max(-1).values >= config.centroid_score_threshold
        print(f"score_pids: Centroid threshold filter applied, idx shape: {idx.shape}", flush=True)

        if self.use_gpu:
            print("score_pids: Processing approx_scores on GPU", flush=True)
            approx_scores = []
            # Filter docs using pruned centroid scores
            for i in range(0, ceil(len(pids) / batch_size)):
                print(f"score_pids: Processing batch {i}", flush=True)
                pids_ = pids[i * batch_size : (i+1) * batch_size]
                codes_packed, codes_lengths = self.embeddings_strided.lookup_codes(pids_)
                idx_ = idx[codes_packed.long()]
                pruned_codes_strided = StridedTensor(idx_, codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
                pruned_codes_padded, pruned_codes_mask = pruned_codes_strided.as_padded_tensor()
                pruned_codes_lengths = (pruned_codes_padded * pruned_codes_mask).sum(dim=1)
                codes_packed_ = codes_packed[idx_]
                approx_scores_ = centroid_scores[codes_packed_.long()]
                if approx_scores_.shape[0] == 0:
                    approx_scores.append(torch.zeros((len(pids_),), dtype=approx_scores_.dtype).cuda())
                    continue
                approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores_, pruned_codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
                approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
                approx_scores_ = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
                approx_scores.append(approx_scores_)
            approx_scores = torch.cat(approx_scores, dim=0)
            assert approx_scores.is_cuda, approx_scores.device
            if config.ndocs < len(approx_scores):
                print("score_pids: Applying topk for pruned docs", flush=True)
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=config.ndocs).indices]

            # Filter docs using full centroid scores
            codes_packed, codes_lengths = self.embeddings_strided.lookup_codes(pids)
            approx_scores = centroid_scores[codes_packed.long()]
            approx_scores_strided = StridedTensor(approx_scores, codes_lengths, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
            approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask = approx_scores_strided.as_padded_tensor()
            approx_scores = colbert_score_reduce(approx_scores_padded, approx_scores_mask, config)
            if config.ndocs // 4 < len(approx_scores):
                pids = pids[torch.topk(approx_scores, k=(config.ndocs // 4)).indices]
        else:
            print("score_pids: CPU branch for centroid_scores", flush=True)
            pids = IndexScorer.filter_pids(
                pids, centroid_scores, self.embeddings.codes, self.doclens,
                self.offsets, idx, config.ndocs
            )
    else:
        print("score_pids: centroid_scores is None", flush=True)
    
    # Rank final list of docs using full approximate embeddings (including residuals)
    if self.use_gpu:
        print("score_pids: Using GPU for final ranking", flush=True)
        print(f"score_pids: pids shape: {pids.shape}", flush=True)
        D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(pids)
        D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    else:
        print("score_pids: Using CPU for final ranking", flush=True)
        D_packed = IndexScorer.decompress_residuals(
            pids,
            self.doclens,
            self.offsets,
            self.codec.bucket_weights,
            self.codec.reversed_bit_map,
            self.codec.decompression_lookup_table,
            self.embeddings.residuals,
            self.embeddings.codes,
            self.codec.centroids,
            self.codec.dim,
            self.codec.nbits
        )
        D_packed = torch.nn.functional.normalize(D_packed.to(torch.float32), p=2, dim=-1)
        D_mask = self.doclens[pids.long()]
        D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    
    # Convert the flat embeddings and mask into padded (non-packed) representation.
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()  # D_padded: [num_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]
    
    # Export the Query and Document tensors for CNN training
    torch.save(Q, "exported_query.pt")                   # Expected shape: [1, query_maxlen, emb_dim] e.g., [1, 32, 128]
    torch.save(D_padded, "exported_doc_padded.pt")         # Expected shape: [num_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]
    torch.save(D_lengths, "exported_doc_lengths.pt")       # Expected shape: [num_docs]
    print("Exported Q, D_padded, and D_lengths for CNN training", flush=True)

    counter += 1
    print(f"Counter: {counter}", flush=True)
    print(f"score_pids: D_packed shape: {D_packed.shape}", flush=True)
    print(f"score_pids: Q shape: {Q.shape}", flush=True)
    print(f"score_pids: D_mask shape: {D_mask.shape}", flush=True)
    print(f"strided_tensor shape: {D_strided.shape}", flush=True)
    print(f"score_pids: D_padded shape: {D_padded.shape}", flush=True)
    
    if Q.size(0) == 1:
        print("score_pids: Using colbert_score_packed", flush=True)
        return colbert_score_packed(Q, D_packed, D_mask, config), pids

    # Otherwise, re-create padded representation (if needed) and use colbert_score.
    D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
    D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()
    print("score_pids: Using colbert_score", flush=True)
    return colbert_score(Q, D_padded, D_lengths, config), pids
````

The code in dense_search uses a configuration branch based on the value of k to adjust the search parameters. In essence:

- For small k (≤ 10):  
  It sets strict parameters (e.g. one cell, a high centroid threshold, and ndocs=256) so that only a small candidate set is produced.

- For medium k (> 10 and ≤ 100):  
  It slightly relaxes the settings (more cells, a lower centroid threshold, ndocs=1024) to allow more candidates.

- For large k (> 100):  
  It uses even looser parameters (e.g. more cells and an even lower threshold) and makes ndocs depend on k (at least k×4 or 4096) so that enough candidates are available for ranking.

This conditional configuration determines how many documents (pids) are later considered for scoring and ranking.

The first dimension of D_padded is not fixed because that tensor comes from the candidate selection and ranking process. In your pipeline (specifically in score_pids), only a subset of all documents is selected for scoring based on threshold filtering and top‑k selection. In other words:

- The candidate generation process (using centroid thresholds and top‑k filtering) decides how many document embeddings (pids) to consider for a given query.  

- D_padded is then formed by padding these candidate document representations to a common length (the maximum token count among the candidates). This is why for one query you might see D_padded with shape [900, 120, 128] while for another it looks like [616, 120, 128].

- The system does not export the embeddings for all documents in the index (e.g. [total_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]) because it is designed to narrow the candidate set before computing similarities (cosine or inner products) or passing them to the CNN.

So, the differences are not due to the scoring method (cosine or CNN) but due to the candidate filtering process, which varies per query based on how many documents pass the threshold. If you wish to export every document embedding before the similarity computation, that would require adjusting the candidate generation to bypass this filtering step.

You can modify the pipeline so that you retrieve (or export) the complete document embedding matrix before any candidate filtering happens. For example, instead of calling lookup_pids(pids) with the filtered candidate IDs, you might retrieve all document IDs (or a larger pool) directly from the index. One approach is to add a branch (or a flag) that bypasses the candidate filtering. For instance, in your score_pids (or in a separate utility), you can do:

````python
# Retrieve all document embeddings (before filtering).
all_pids = torch.arange(0, len(self.doclens), device=Q.device)
D_packed, D_mask = self.lookup_pids(all_pids)
D_strided = StridedTensor(D_packed, D_mask, use_gpu=self.use_gpu)
D_padded, D_lengths = D_strided.as_padded_tensor()
torch.save(D_padded, "exported_all_doc_padded.pt")      # Shape: [total_docs, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]
torch.save(D_lengths, "exported_all_doc_lengths.pt")
print("Exported all documents embeddings for CNN training")
````

This code bypasses the candidate filtering so that you export a tensor shaped like [number_of_all_documents, max_doc_tokens, emb_dim]. You could place this code once (for example, before running the search pipeline) or condition it on a flag. 

Note that if you do this on the fly per query, the exported D may vary with the candidate filtering. Bypassing filtering ensures that the exported D represents the full index.

response.value:
The call

  torch.zeros((1, config.query_maxlen, config.emb_dim))

creates a dummy query tensor that defines the expected dimensions. In this case, the dimensions are used for:

• Setting the maximum number of query tokens (config.query_maxlen)  
• Matching the embedding dimensions (config.emb_dim)

This dummy tensor is only used by the export_all_documents method to know the correct shape for downstream processing (for example, when processing document embeddings in the same format as query embeddings). If you skipped these values, the system wouldn’t know what dimensions to expect for the query and document embeddings when exporting them for CNN training or other tasks. 

If you prefer not to use config values directly, you can hardcode the dimensions—provided you’re sure they match the model’s expectations. However, the parameters are necessary to ensure that the exported tensors are correctly shaped for later use.
